text: Again he began to teach beside the sea. Such a huge crowd gathered around him that he got into a boat and sat in it out on the water, while the whole crowd was on the shore at the water's edge.
He taught them many things in parables, and in his teaching he said to them:
"Listen! A sower went out to sow.

versions.text: "Listen! A farmer went out to sow.
versions.explanation: The Greek ὁ σπείρων is rendered "the sower" in verse 14 ("The sower sows the word"), which is the explanation of this very parable. Using "farmer" here breaks the link the parable's interpretation depends on. Keeping "sower" preserves the internal consistency and the wordplay of "sower ... sow."

text: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.
Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it had little soil. It sprang up at once, because the soil was shallow,
but when the sun rose it was scorched, and since it had no root, it withered away.
Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, so it produced no crop.

versions.text: Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, so it produced no grain.
versions.explanation: καρπόν is the same word rendered "crop" in verse 8 and "fruit" in verse 20; "grain" narrows the image unnecessarily and breaks consistency within the parable.

text: And other seed fell on good soil. It came up, grew, and produced a crop—thirty, sixty, even a hundred times what was sown."
And he said, "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear."
When he was alone, those around him, along with the Twelve, asked him about the parables.
He told them, "To you has been given the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to those outside everything comes in parables,
so that they may look and look, yet never see, and hear and hear, yet never understand; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven."
Then he said to them, "Don't you understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of them?
The sower sows the word.
Some people are like the seed along the path, where the word is sown: as soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
Others are like the seed sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they receive it at once with joy,
but they have no root in themselves and last only a little while. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately fall away.
Others are like the seed sown among thorns. These are the ones who hear the word,
but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the craving for other things come in and choke the word, and it produces nothing.
But those sown on good soil are the ones who hear the word, welcome it, and bear fruit—thirty, sixty, even a hundred times what was sown."
He also said to them, "Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed? Doesn't he put it on a stand?
For nothing is hidden except to be revealed, and nothing is concealed except to be brought out into the open.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear."
And he said to them, "Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you—and more besides.

versions.text: And he said to them, "Pay attention to what you hear. The measure you use will be used for you, and you will be given even more.
versions.explanation: The Greek repeats the root μετρ- ("measure... will be measured"), a deliberate echo that carries well in oral reading. "The measure you use will be used for you" flattens this and is slightly ambiguous.

text: For to the one who has, more will be given; and from the one who has nothing, even what he has will be taken away."
He also said, "The kingdom of God is like this: a man scatters seed on the ground.
Night and day he sleeps and rises, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how.
All by itself the earth bears fruit: first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
And when the grain is ripe, he takes the sickle at once, because the harvest has come."
And he said, "How shall we picture the kingdom of God? What parable shall we use for it?
It is like a mustard seed. When it is sown in the ground, it is the smallest of all the seeds on earth,
yet once it is sown it comes up and becomes the largest of all the garden plants, with branches so big that the birds of the sky can nest in its shade."
With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as much as they were able to hear.
He did not speak to them without a parable, but privately he explained everything to his own disciples.
That day, when evening came, he said to them, "Let's cross over to the other side."
So they left the crowd behind and took him with them in the boat, just as he was. Other boats went along with him.
A fierce squall came up, and the waves broke over the boat, so that it was already being swamped.
Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on a cushion. They woke him and said, "Teacher, don't you care that we're going to drown?"
He got up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, "Quiet! Be still!" The wind died down, and there was a great calm.
He said to them, "Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?"
They were terrified and said to one another, "Who is this? Even the wind and the sea obey him!"
